REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - AUGUST 28, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.gov or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.gov in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments will be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the legislative body, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a legislative body member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to cancel or reschedule a City Council public meeting.

If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council/Successor Agency will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, AUGUST 28, 2025,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD
AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Bishop David Montgomery, Church of Jesus Christ Latter-
  Day Saints.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Girl Scout Troop 313.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jennifer Hong
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Council/Agency Member Sophia M. Tse
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Lynda P. Johnson
  Mayor/Chair Frank Aurelio Yokoyama

  ADDITION OF URGENCY ITEM TO AGENDA:

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, stated that due to a matter of urgency that came before the City
  of Cerritos (City) after the posting of the agenda for the Thursday, August 28, 2025, 7:00
  p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting, the City Council should take action to
  amend the agenda to add Item 12C to consider a matter of potential litigation. This item
  requires consideration by the City Council prior to the next scheduled meeting on
  Monday, September 8, 2025, 7:00 p.m. Pursuant to California Government Code Section
  54954.2(b)(2), to add this item to tonight’s agenda, the City Council must move and approve
  to find (i) that an urgency item came to the attention of the City of Cerritos after the posting
  of the agenda for tonight’s meeting; and (ii) there is a need to take immediate action before
  the next City Council meeting.

  (minutes continue on the next page)
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 28, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 11

ADDITION OF URGENCY ITEM TO AGENDA (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Hong, to:

  1. Make the findings that:

  a. An urgency item came to the attention of the City of Cerritos after the posting of the
  agenda for the Thursday, August 28, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency
  Regular Meeting; and

  b. The matter requires prompt action by the City Council, prior to the next scheduled City
  Council meeting at 7:00 p.m. on Monday, September 8, 2025; and

  2. The agenda for the Thursday, August 28, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency
  Regular Meeting should be amended to add the item listed below as an urgency item,
  pursuant to California Government Code Section 54954.2(b)(2):

  12C.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - POTENTIAL LITIGATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(1) (COUNCIL)
  Number of Potential Cases: One (1)

  ; (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  Mayor Yokoyama requested a moment of silence in remembrance of the Cerritos Air
  Disaster as August 31, 2025, marks the 39th anniversary of the event.

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Trader Joe’s (Business Spotlight).

5B.  Review and consideration of City Council appointments to the Cerritos Advisory Boards
  (Boards, Commissions, and Committees) (2025-2027 term) (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the
  public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve Councilmember
  Pulido’s nomination listed below for a two-year term of service, through April 30, 2027
  (COUNCIL):

  Name  Advisory Board
  Aris Tagle  Economic Development Commission
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, August 28, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 3 of 11

5.  Presentations/Appointments (continued)

5B.  (continued)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, administered the oath of office to appointee Aris Tagle.

5C.  Review and consideration of the Mayor’s nominations for appointments to internal ad hoc
  working groups and external boards, commissions, and committees (COUNCIL).

  Pursuant to City Council consensus, consideration of this item was deferred to the next
  City Council/Successor Agency meeting agenda (scheduled for Monday, September 8,
  2025).

  There were no public comments received on this item and no action was taken.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Linda Troxell expressed concern regarding the current state of her home and requested
  assistance in securing toxic substance remediation services.

  Case Van der Linden spoke in opposition of a water rate increase and of the extending of
  the terminus of the Southeast Gateway Line light rail transit stop to the Orange County
  line. He also spoke in opposition of rezoning at Del Amo Boulevard and Pioneer
  Boulevard, to accommodate more housing.

  David Pylman expressed support for the creation of a Senior Services Commission and/or
  a Disability Advisory Committee.

  The Mayor announced that prior to the meeting, the Council/Agency members received
  full-text, unredacted copies of the four (4) written comments submitted for Item 6, by
  the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the official record. Requests for
  copies of the written comments submitted for this meeting can be made during regular
  business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7C.  Continuance of the existence of a local emergency concerning a gasoline leak from a
  privately owned existing pipeline on the Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine public golf course, and
  potential threat to the safety of persons and property requiring remediation, repair, and
  improvement of the public golf course and other City-owned public property, as specified
  (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Tse, to:

  1. Continue the local emergency as proclaimed in Resolution No. 2023-05, at the
  Cerritos Iron-Wood Nine Golf Course and the nearby City property containing the C-4
  well site;

  2. Make the findings set forth in Sections one (1) through eight (8) of Resolution No.
  2023-05, and incorporate by reference those findings, as they relate to the continued
  existence of a local emergency as specified; and

  3. Direct staff to provide a report to the City Council regarding the local emergency at
  least once every sixty (60) days, pursuant to Section 8630(c) of the California
  Government Code, until the City Council terminates the local emergency (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Hong, Pulido, Tse, Johnson, Yokoyama
  NOES:  None

  ABSTAIN:  None

  for the Lower San Gabriel River and Los Cerritos Channel Watershed Management

  required for compliance with the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System

9.  New and Old Business

REORDERING OF THE AGENDA
At this juncture, the City Council, by consensus, reordered the agenda to consider New and Old
Business Item 9B prior to consideration of Item 9A.

9A.  Review and consideration of proposed sewer rate adjustment options to support long-
  term fiscal sustainability (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Chris Kuebert, Assistant Director of Public Works. A
  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  David Pylman expressed concern regarding the total number of attendees permitted to
  attend the upcoming Community Open House events scheduled at the City’s Corporate
  Yard, and stated he hoped additional attendees would be permitted to attend the event
  scheduled at the Cerritos Senior Center. He also requested the City include the City of La
  Palma when surveying surrounding cities’ sewer rates, as a number of Cerritos residents
  are billed by the City of La Palma for sewer use.

  Kirit Chauhan expressed appreciation for the clear and concise manner by which the
  agenda report for this item was presented. He also inquired regarding aspects of water
  and sewer billing and expressed support for a gradual rate increase over time.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Johnson, and seconded by Tse, to:

  1. Approve progression of the sewer rate adjustment process in accordance with
  Scenario 1, as presented in the agenda report associated with this item, with General
  Fund support, phased out over five (5) fiscal years, and fixed residential and
  commercial sewer rate unit charges (customers are charged per one hundred cubic
  feet (CCF) of water usage for sewer collection services), as follows:

  General Fund Support to Sewer Fund
  Fiscal Year  Fiscal Year  Fiscal Year  Fiscal Year  Fiscal Year

  Commercial and Residential Sewer Rates

  cubic feet  2026  2027  2028  2029  2030
  (CCF)

  and;

  2. Direct staff to finalize the sewer rate study report accordingly and present the final
  report for City Council review and consideration at a future meeting (COUNCIL).

11B.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports

  Reports were given by Councilmembers Tse, Hong, and Pulido, Mayor Pro Tem Johnson,
  and Mayor Yokoyama.

  CONSENSUS (Johnson): Directed the City Manager to: 1. Initiate a communications
  campaign using various City communication platforms to solicit bona fide nonprofit
  501(c)(3) organizations interested in establishing a Sister City program to submit a
  request to the City Manager’s Office, in accordance with City Policy No. 7.07; and 2.
  Schedule a report for City Council consideration of approval of the request(s) submitted,
  with subsequent review by the Economic Development Commission, as directed by the
  City Council.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Directed the City Manager to examine and investigate
  establishing a partnership with the City of Artesia to utilize a combined network of
  automatic license plate reader (ALPR) cameras within both agencies, for improved safety
  services.
